_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4b, IC4-R1). `pairs` is the plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides. The confused pairings (Ney/Lannes, Massena/Davout) drawn twice each.

who.Ney: Ney — a bold marshal, famous for his courage and his impatience to fight.
who.Davout: Davout — a careful marshal, strict, exact, who counts every man and never wastes one.
who.Murat: Murat — a bold cavalry marshal who loves to ride and charge.
who.Lannes: Lannes — a bold marshal who marches to the sound of the guns and leads assaults himself.
who.Massena: Masséna — a stubborn marshal who never gives up ground he holds.
who.Bernadotte: Bernadotte — a slow, politic marshal who is never in a hurry and always has an excuse.

pairs.line1: No task, Sire? I'll find a fight myself now, before I go mad sitting here.
pairs.line2: As I see fit, Sire. Wherever the guns are loudest, that's where you'll find me.

pairs.line1: I failed, Sire. Straight talk: I'll lead the assault again.
pairs.line2: It went badly, Sire. Give me another go; I'd sooner be fighting than brooding.

pairs.line1: Leave me here, Sire. This is my ground, and they pay for every yard.
pairs.line2: Let me hold here, Sire, with every company counted and in place.

pairs.line1: Carefully, Sire. Every man and every wagon in its place.
pairs.line2: Careful, yes. Not an inch of my ground is lost that way.

pairs.line1: No fight today, and not a yard of mine lost by waiting.
pairs.line2: Still nothing to fight, Sire. The men are restless, and so am I.

pairs.line1: No hurry today, Sire. I'm sure tomorrow will do just as well.
pairs.line2: No fight today. Everything is in its place.

pairs.line1: I don't like leaving a place I've made mine, Sire. I'll go if I must.
pairs.line2: Straight out, Sire: I'd not choose this. I'll do it all the same, with my ear on the guns.

pairs.line1: Last time I was called back, Sire, no doubt for good reasons. I'd like to finish this one, in my own good time.
pairs.line2: Last time your order kept my columns from a friend's fight. I remember it.

pairs.line1: Done, Sire. Point me at the next one and I'll ride.
pairs.line2: The task is done, Sire. Now give me something worth fighting.

pairs.line1: It did not succeed, Sire. Circumstances were against me.
pairs.line2: I let you down, Sire. Give me a horse and another try.

pairs.line1: I can do no more here without orders, Sire. Every man stays where he is.
pairs.line2: Tell me where to ride, Sire.

rows.line: I regret it, Sire. The conditions were poor.
I failed, Sire. Straight talk: I'll lead the assault again.
I did not manage it, Sire. I'll go over the figures to find my fault.
It went wrong, Sire. I held my ground as long as I could.
The ride did not go as I pictured it, Sire.
It went badly, Sire. Give me another go; I'd sooner be fighting than brooding.
Let me dig in here, Sire, and see every man fed and in his place.
Let me hold here, Sire, though I can't sit long. The first enemy who shows will regret it.
Nothing worth chasing yet, Sire. Let me hold here with the horses saddled.
Let me hold my front, Sire, and strike out from it when I see the chance.
I could hold where I am, Sire. Quiet work, and safe.
I'll hold here with the columns ready, Sire, and my ear on the guns.
Careful is wise, Sire. I agree entirely.
Carefully. I'd already counted the men and the stores, Sire.
Carefully — if you say so. I'll go to the guns all the same.
Carefully? Very well, Sire, but I can't bear it long, and I go in the moment I can.
Carefully... the horses won't like it, but very well.
Careful, yes. Not an inch of my ground is lost that way.
Your order, Sire. My own chase can wait a day.
Your order first, Sire. My task is noted and will be resumed with every man in his place.
Your order first, Sire. The guns can hold off a day for me.
Your order first, of course, Sire. My task can wait, and I'm in no rush.
Your order comes first, Sire. My task waits, and I'm chafing already.
Very well. My task stays mine, and I'll come back to it.
I did not wait, Sire. You know I never do.
I struck when the figures were right, Sire. Not before.
I heard guns and went, Sire. You would have done the same.
I attacked, as it happens, Sire. I hope you understand it could not be helped.
They came too near my ground, so I hit them.
We charged today, Sire. Sabres out, plumes up, a fine sight.
